module.title: Bacterial lipoprotein maturation
module.description: A bacterial envelope-biogenesis module for the ordered maturation of lipobox-containing prolipoproteins: Lgt diacylglyceryl transfer, LspA (signal peptidase II) cleavage of the signal peptide, and, in diderm lineages, Lnt N-acylation to give triacylated lipoproteins. The Lgt and LspA steps are pan-bacterial and are grounded here in Escherichia coli K-12, Pseudomonas putida KT2440 and Bacillus subtilis 168; the Lnt step is optional and lineage-restricted, grounded in E. coli and P. putida. Lol sorting to the outer membrane and substrate-specific lipoprotein functions are downstream and outside this module.

module.notes: Reusable boundary: this module models maturation chemistry, not all proteins that later act as mature lipoproteins. Lgt and LspA are present in diderm and monoderm bacteria alike (E. coli, P. putida and B. subtilis are the representatives), and in each lineage LspA cleaves only after Lgt has lipidated the lipobox cysteine. The Lnt step is marked optional: the cached PTHR38686 member inventory has no Firmicutes member, so B. subtilis lipoproteins remain diacylated or are N-modified by non-orthologous enzymes that are not modelled here; actinobacterial Lnt is fused to a Ppm1 mannosyltransferase domain whose activity is outside this module. Essentiality differs between lineages (lgt and lspA are essential in E. coli but not in B. subtilis), which reflects downstream outer-membrane sorting requirements, not differences in enzyme activity. Curation notes: GO lacks specific lipoprotein signal peptidase and apolipoprotein N-acyltransferase activity terms, so the LspA and Lnt steps use GO:0004190 and GO:0016747 and the gene reviews carry proposed new terms. The P. putida PP_4236/Q88F63 DsbE/CcmG-like protein, which carries an Lgt-like propagated label in the species-aware UPA00664 report, is not counted as an Lgt. The KEGG partition places lspA in ppu03060 Protein export, so an automated UPA00665 candidate list shows only lspA; that is a partitioning artifact, not a missing step. Downstream Lol trafficking is the separate bacterial_lol_lipoprotein_trafficking module.

document.summary: Lnt enzymes are cytoplasmic-membrane N-acyltransferases with a periplasmic nitrilase-like (CN hydrolase) catalytic domain. They transfer an acyl chain from a glycerophospholipid to the free amino group of the diacylglyceryl cysteine of apolipoproteins, the terminal step of lipoprotein maturation in Proteobacteria and other diderms. The family is restricted in phylogenetic range compared with Lgt and LspA: the cached member inventory (reviewed UniProt entries) contains no Firmicutes member, B. subtilis included, and actinobacteria carry members fused to a Ppm1 polyprenol-phosphate mannose synthase domain (M. tuberculosis O53493). PANTHER defines one subfamily (SF1) holding all members.
